test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In January 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lifted restrictions on which two Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arohan and Muthoot Finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, on **January 1, 2025**, announced the lifting of business restrictions on two prominent **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**.
 
• The curbs were removed for **Arohan Financial Services Limited** and **Asirvad Microfinance Limited**, which is a key subsidiary of **Muthoot Finance**. *Hence, the statement regarding Arohan and Muthoot Finance is correct.*
 
• These restrictions were originally imposed in **October 2024** due to concerns regarding **usurious interest rates** and non-compliance with the **regulatory framework** for microfinance loans.
 
• The **RBI** had issued a "cease and desist" order, which prevented these companies from **sanctioning and disbursing** new loans, although they were allowed to continue servicing existing accounts.
 
• The lifting of the ban followed significant **corrective actions** taken by the companies, including restructuring their **pricing policies** and interest rate models to align with **RBI** guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Asirvad Microfinance Limited:** Headquartered in **Chennai**, it is one of India's largest **NBFC-MFIs**. It was acquired by **Muthoot Finance** in **2015** and serves millions of women entrepreneurs in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• **Arohan Financial Services Limited:** Based in **Kolkata**, it is a leading microfinance institution in **Eastern India**. It provides credit, insurance, and pension products to the **underbanked population**.
 
• **October 2024 RBI Action:** The **RBI** had taken action against four entities: **Asirvad Microfinance**, **Arohan Financial Services**, **Navi Finserv**, and **DMI Finance**. The central bank cited **high interest rates** that were not in proportion to the cost of funds and risk profiles.
 
• **Fair Practices Code:** The **RBI** mandates that all **NBFCs** follow a code that ensures transparency in loan pricing and prohibits **predatory lending** practices.
 
• **Impact on Sector:** The lifting of restrictions in **January 2025** is seen as a positive signal for the **microfinance sector**, indicating that regulatory compliance can lead to the restoration of business operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, specifically **Section 45L**, empowers the **RBI** to issue directions to **NBFCs** to ensure the financial system's stability.
 
• In **2024**, the **RBI** intensified its supervision of **NBFC-MFIs** due to reports of high **household indebtedness** and aggressive recovery methods.
 
• The **Weighted Average Lending Rate (WALR)** is a critical metric monitored by the **RBI** to ensure that the **benefits of lower interest rates** are passed on to end-consumers.
 
• The **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN)**, a self-regulatory organization, has also introduced a **Code of Conduct** to prevent over-leveraging of borrowers in the **unorganized sector**.
